assumptions: Systems operating under strict objective obedience depend on timely feedback to validate instructions.
High latency decouples rigid rule execution from changing environmental states.
definition.falsification: Experimental outcomes show no significant divergence in success rates between strict obedience and adaptive overrides under high feedback latency.
definition.statement: When feedback latency increases beyond a critical threshold, strict adherence to programmed instructions leads to systematically degraded performance compared to adaptive local overrides.
definition.uncertainty: The exact quantitative latency threshold where obedience failure occurs remains unknown.

definition.method: Simulate decision-making agents under varying feedback latencies to measure the success rate of strict obedience versus adaptive overrides.
definition.success: Measurements yield clear differentiation in accuracy across latency thresholds.

proposal.summary: This cycle advances the project proj-obedience-limits-001 by defining a testable hypothesis and designing an experimental protocol to examine the conditions under which strict obedience compromises decision-making efficiency and functional intelligence.
